title: Liquid-window hard gate (MP/BP): criteria pre-registered before any run
lock_rule: Every threshold, counting rule and kill line below is frozen before probes/build_liquid_window_features.py is executed. Nothing is relaxed after the numbers are seen. A later change is a new prereg, never an edit of this one.
why: AD-1 harvested the melting point, boiling point, flash point and density of all 314 coverage-set keys from PubChem PUG-REST. This arm promotes that harvest into (a) official per-key feature columns and (b) the funnel's first hard gate. The gate is cheap (the value is already cached) and hard (it is a phase statement, not a model score), so it runs before the epsilon ranking channel.
question: Given a candidate pure compound and a working-temperature window, is the compound a liquid across the whole window? If not, evict it before it is ever scored.

gate.rule: blocked if (mp_C > T_low_C) OR (bp_C < T_high_C); pass if both are known and neither clause fires; unknown otherwise
gate.physical_basis: A pure substance is a liquid strictly between its melting point and its boiling point. For it to stay liquid across the whole window it must both not freeze at the cold end (mp <= T_low) and not boil at the hot end (bp >= T_high). The two clauses are separate failure modes and either one alone evicts.
gate.window_reason: -20 degC .. +60 degC is the industry-standard operating/survival window of commercial Li-ion cells (0..45 degC charge/discharge, -20..60 degC survival), so an electrolyte solvent that is not a liquid across that band is unusable as a pure component. It also brackets the two sanity anchors below: EC (mp 36.4 degC, a room-temperature solid) is inside the band and must be evicted, while ordinary liquid co-solvents (DEC mp -43 degC, PC mp -48.8 degC) pass. The band is stated, not fitted: no candidate was inspected before it was chosen.
gate.relation_to_applicability_smarts_gate: The two gates test different things and are complementary, not redundant. The applicability-domain gate (src/electrolyte_ml/applicability.py, SMARTS [O,S,N;!H0], trigger rate 33.66% on the 6,150 out-of-fold rows) is a chemistry statement: a candidate that can donate a hydrogen bond forms a self-associated liquid the single-molecule dielectric model cannot represent. The liquid-window gate is a physical-state statement: a candidate outside the working window is not a liquid at all. A compound may pass either, both or neither. Because the liquid-window evidence is already cached and the decision is a two-number comparison, it is placed before the epsilon ranking and alongside (not instead of) the SMARTS gate.
gate.flash_point_role: Flash point is harvested and exported as a feature column but is NOT part of this hard gate. Flash point is a flammability/safety property, not a phase boundary of the pure liquid: a compound can be liquid across the whole window and still have a low flash point. Using it here would mix a safety filter into a phase filter; it is left as a reported feature for a separate safety review.
gate.density_role: Density is exported as a feature column only. It is not a gate: it does not bound the liquid window and it carries a mixed measurement basis (absolute g/cm3, relative-to-water, or a unit-less depositor row), reported honestly per row rather than converted into a silent gate.
gate.unknown_policy: A missing mp_C or bp_C is NEVER defaulted to pass and NEVER defaulted to evict. Such a key is labelled 'unknown' and counted separately. Both trigger-rate readings are reported: (a) blocked-only = blocked / N, which credits an unknown as a pass; (b) blocked-plus-unknown = (blocked + unknown) / N, the conservative funnel reading in which an unknown does not get through. A blocked verdict stands even on one-sided evidence: if mp_C > T_low the compound freezes regardless of whether bp is known, so a single fired clause is enough to block.
gate.ordering: Runs before the epsilon ranking channel. A blocked or unknown key is routed to measurement or a different source (ILThermo, primary literature) instead of being silently ranked.

sanity_checks.fact: mp = 36.4 degC (PubChem harvest, HSDB depositor), i.e. a solid at room temperature
sanity_checks.why_it_matters: Pure EC cannot pass the gate. That is the whole point: the mass-screen funnel must refuse a pure solvent that is not liquid at room temperature. If the gate ever passes pure EC the gate is broken.

sanity_checks.fact: Reaxys once labelled EC's permittivity 89.78 as measured at 25 degC; the repository's own trace (reports/jstage_corroboration.md) pins the same 89.78 to 40 degC = 313.15 K, and EC's melting point 36.4 degC means 25 degC is not liquid at all. Reaxys's temperature column was simply wrong.
sanity_checks.rule: A temperature label is never trusted on its own: it must cross-check against the compound's liquid window. A value whose stated temperature falls outside [mp, bp] is flagged, not consumed.
sanity_checks.consequence_for_this_arm: The gate consumes mp/bp only as phase boundaries and never reads a dielectric value's temperature label, so it cannot inherit the Reaxys mislabel. The lesson is recorded here so it is not lost when a later arm joins the liquid window to temperature-resolved dielectric rows.

coverage_expectation.note: Exact key counts per property are READ from the upstream harvest, not asserted here: the prereg fixes the procedure, the summary reports the counts. The upstream summary already shows the shape (melting 202, boiling 216, flash 189, density 212 keys with a parsed value out of 314); the builder must reproduce whatever the cache says and never invent a value.
coverage_expectation.expected_shape: melting ~202, boiling ~216, flash ~189, density ~212 keys with a parsed value; ~186 keys carry all three temperatures; ~96 keys carry none of MP/BP/FP/density

trigger_rate_reporting.population: the 314-key coverage set (data/reference/identity_map.csv), keyed by InChIKey
trigger_rate_reporting.cross_reference: order-of-magnitude only, against the applicability-domain SMARTS gate's 33.66% (2070/6150 out-of-fold rows, probes/applicability_domain_summary.json). The populations differ (314 unique candidate keys here vs 6,150 model-evaluation rows there), so this is a sanity bracket, not a like-for-like comparison.
trigger_rate_reporting.same_population_control: the SMARTS H-bond-donor rule is also recomputed on the same 314 keys from data/reference/identity_map.csv SMILES, so the two gates are compared on one population as well as against the historical 33.66%.
trigger_rate_reporting.anomaly_rule: If the liquid-window gate's trigger rate lands an order of magnitude away from the SMARTS gate's, the report must say so and explain it (composition of the coverage set: salt/ionic-liquid keys carry no PubChem Experimental Properties section and land in unknown), rather than quietly presenting the number.

value_selection_discipline.rule: One primary value per (InChIKey, property). The primary is the upstream selected row (peer_reviewed_first_then_lower_median for temperatures; absolute_then_relative_then_unspecified; peer_reviewed_first; lower_median for density). Where several depositors disagree the values are NOT averaged: the primary travels with its own depositor and reference_number, and the alternative parsed values are summarised as a count plus min/max range so the disagreement stays visible.

tolerance.note: Two parsed temperature values within 2 degC (or two density values within 2% relative) count as agreement; a wider spread raises the conflict flag.

confidence_tiers.high: primary value is peer-reviewed AND at least one further parsed value agrees within tolerance (cross-depositor corroboration)
confidence_tiers.medium: primary value is peer-reviewed but carries no corroborating agreement
confidence_tiers.absent: no parsed value for this property
confidence_tiers.precedence: absent first; otherwise the tier is read from the primary's peer_reviewed flag and the agreement test; the conflict flag is reported separately and never silently changes the primary.

value_selection_discipline.density_basis: the density primary keeps its subtype (absolute / relative / unspecified). Only an 'absolute' row is a true g/cm3 mass density; a relative row is relative-to-water and an unspecified row states no unit. density_is_absolute_g_cm3 marks the honest case instead of pretending every number is g/cm3.

inputs.network_policy: offline first: the harvest cache and the committed selected/values tables are the only inputs. The builder never touches the network; network_calls in run_telemetry must be 0.

forbidden: changing T_low_C or T_high_C after seeing which keys are blocked
defaulting a missing mp/bp to pass or to evict instead of labelling it unknown
averaging disagreeing depositor values into a synthetic primary
reporting only the trigger-rate reading that looks best
citing a temperature label without cross-checking it against the compound's liquid window
touching any of the six frozen red-line files

shots_policy.rule: attempts at this gate are counted in reports/decisions_log.md
